questions.q: What is the Brain, in one line?
options: A shared industry database every Zoca business contributes facts to
A per-business memory layer storing owner-approved facts that grounds every Zoca AI
A standalone chatbot that replaces the front-desk phone line
A generic AI writing tool like ChatGPT for marketing copy
questions.explain: The Brain is a per-business memory layer that stores facts the owner has approved and serves them to every Zoca AI.

questions.q: Why does fixing one fact in the Brain improve every Zoca tool at once?
options: Because each tool keeps its own copy that syncs nightly
Because the owner manually pushes updates to each AI
Because all five Zoca AIs read from the same Brain
Because only the website and Front Desk share facts
questions.explain: All five Zoca AIs read from the same Brain, so correcting one fact makes every tool better at once.

questions.q: Which is one of the three foundation principles of how the Brain works?
options: Facts are pooled and shared to train other owners' AIs
Per-business ownership — a Brain belongs to one business and is never shared
Facts are auto-confirmed without owner review to save time
The Brain stays fixed and never changes after setup
questions.explain: Per-business ownership means a Brain belongs to one business and is never pooled or shared.

questions.q: According to the lesson, can owners control whether a fact is used per-tool today (e.g., on calls but not the blog)?
options: Yes, per-surface control is fully available now
No — per-tool control isn't possible yet; a fact is available to all tools
Yes, but only for pricing facts
Only staff accounts can set per-tool rules
questions.explain: Per-tool control is a known gap; today a confirmed fact is available to all tools, so don't promise per-surface control.

questions.q: Which tab is the visual topic map of every confirmed fact and the demo's 'wow shot'?
options: Canvas
Validate
Preview
Memory History
questions.explain: Canvas is the visual topic map of all confirmed facts and is opened first as the wow shot.

questions.q: What are the four actions an owner can take on a card in the Validate tab?
options: Approve, Pause, Archive, Delete
Confirm, Refine, Edit, Reject
Accept, Flag, Merge, Restore
Confirm, Share, Edit, Export
questions.explain: The four Validate actions are Confirm, Refine, Edit, and Reject.

questions.q: What does the Preview tab let an owner do?
options: Schedule when facts go live
Type a customer question and see the exact grounded answer with citations to the facts used
Bulk-import an FAQ list
Compare their Brain to a competitor's
questions.explain: Preview lets you type any customer question and see the exact grounded answer with citations to the Brain facts it used.

questions.q: Why do compliance-minded buyers care about Memory History?
options: It hides facts from staff members
It auto-deletes old facts after 30 days
It's a complete, dated, attributed, exportable audit trail of every fact with one-click restore
It blocks the AI from answering until reviewed
questions.explain: Memory History is a complete, dated, attributed audit trail that is exportable, with one-click restore — exactly what compliance asks for.

questions.q: What are the Brain's two learning paths?
options: Path A KNOWN (AI confirms an answer it has) and Path B UNKNOWN (it becomes a question to answer)
Automatic scraping and manual entry
Owner path and staff path
Daily crawl and weekly crawl
questions.explain: Path A (KNOWN) drops a confirmation into Validate; Path B (UNKNOWN) becomes a question in the Question Bank to answer.

questions.q: Which sources are read ONCE at onboarding to seed the Brain?
options: Command Center chats and the nightly gap-scan
Your website, Google Business Profile, past call transcripts, and existing Zoca data
Generated blog and social posts
Competitor websites and Yelp reviews only
questions.explain: Website, Google profile, past calls, and existing Zoca data are read once at onboarding to seed the Brain — there is no nightly re-crawl.

questions.q: When a new candidate fact contradicts an existing fact, what does the Brain do?
options: Silently overwrites with the newer fact
Keeps the older fact and ignores the new one
Flags the conflict and offers a three-way choice: replace, keep both, or cancel
Deletes both facts to avoid errors
questions.explain: The Brain never silently overwrites; it flags the conflict and offers replace, keep both, or cancel.

questions.q: What is the cap on the AI work behind the Brain?
options: $50 per month per location
$50 per month per business
$100 per month per location
There is no cap
questions.explain: AI costs are capped at $50 per month per location, a safety ceiling so an owner can't run up a bill.

questions.q: What is the strict 5-minute demo path through the tabs?
options: Question Bank → Canvas → Preview → Validate
Canvas → Validate → Preview → Memory History
Validate → Memory History → Canvas → Preview
Canvas → Question Bank → Preview → Validate
questions.explain: The strict path is Canvas (wow shot) → Validate (confirm live) → Preview (cited answer) → Memory History (audit close).

questions.q: Which is the single most powerful demo moment?
options: Touring all five tabs thoroughly
Explaining how the engine works under the hood
Steps 3 and 4 back-to-back: the owner confirms a fact, then watches it come out of the AI cited
Showing the $50 cost cap first
questions.explain: Handing them the mouse to confirm a fact, then immediately seeing it cited in Preview, is 'the click' the demo is built around.

questions.q: Which is one of the three NEVER-SAY over-promises?
options: "You're in control of every fact"
"The AI will never hallucinate"
"Each card takes about 30 seconds"
"Your Brain is private to your business"
questions.explain: 'The AI will never hallucinate' is a NEVER-SAY; say instead it grounds against approved facts and is scored to catch drift.

questions.q: If an owner asks about time-bound offers, per-surface control, or other languages, how should you handle it?
options: Demo it as live to impress them
Promise a specific delivery date
Say 'coming soon' but don't demo it as live or commit a date
Tell them it will never be built
questions.explain: These are roadmap items: it's fine to say 'coming soon,' but do not demo them as live or promise a date.

questions.q: How should you pitch the Brain at the highest level?
options: "It's a free AI chatbot for your website"
"Train your AI once, the way you'd train a great new receptionist"
"It shares your best facts with the Zoca network"
"Set it and forget it forever"
questions.explain: The core pitch is to train your AI once the way you'd train a great new receptionist.

questions.q: How many Zoca AIs does the Brain power?
options: Three
Four
Five
Seven
questions.explain: The Brain powers five Zoca AIs: Front Desk, Website, Content, Google Profile, and Command Center.

questions.q: What is the 'source pill' on a Validate card?
options: A confidence score for the fact
A chip showing where the candidate fact came from (call, website, Google, chat, staff save)
A button that confirms the fact
A timer showing when the fact expires
questions.explain: The source pill is the chip on each candidate showing where the fact came from so the owner can judge whether to trust it.

questions.q: Which tab lets an owner test the AI's answer the way a customer would, with citations?
options: Canvas
Question Bank
Preview
Memory History
questions.explain: Preview lets you ask a customer-style question and see the exact grounded answer with citations.

questions.q: What does NOT feed back into the Brain as new facts?
options: Command Center chats
Content the AI generates, like its own blog and social posts
Past call transcripts at onboarding
Questions the owner answers
questions.explain: Content the AI generates is deliberately not fed back in; the Brain is built on the owner's confirmed facts, not the AI's own output.

questions.q: Roughly how much time does keeping the Brain current take?
options: About 30 seconds per card and about five minutes a week
About an hour a day
A full afternoon at onboarding, then nothing
Several hours a week
questions.explain: Each fact takes roughly 30 seconds to review and most owners spend about five minutes a week.

questions.q: Who can confirm a fact into the Brain today?
options: Any staff member
Only the owner; staff can save candidates but not approve
Anyone with the link
Zoca support, on the owner's behalf
questions.explain: Today only the owner confirms a fact, by design for a consistent voice; staff can save candidates with one click.

questions.q: How should you answer 'My business changes all the time — won't this get stale?'
options: "We re-crawl your website every night to stay fresh"
"It stays current through how you use Zoca — Command Center chats, answered questions, and a nightly gap-scan"
"You'll need to re-import everything monthly"
"It can't stay current; that's a known limitation"
questions.explain: Freshness is usage-driven via Command Center chats, answered questions, saves, and a nightly gap-scan — not a nightly re-crawl.

questions.q: What is the core distinction the lesson uses to define Command Center?
options: It only answers questions about the salon's data
It performs actions on the salon's behalf, not just answers questions
It replaces the Front Desk AI entirely
It is a separate mobile-only app
questions.explain: Command Center performs actions in plain language rather than merely giving advice, which the lesson calls the whole point.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut opens Command Center from any page?
options: Cmd+K
Cmd+J
Ctrl+Space
Cmd+Enter
questions.explain: The lesson states Cmd+K is the shortcut to open Command Center instantly from anywhere.

questions.q: What are the three things behind every Command Center reply?
options: Calendar, billing, and reviews
Voice, text, and email
Knowledge base, action toolkit, and memory/Brain
Read, write, and confirm
questions.explain: Every request draws on the knowledge base, the action toolkit, and memory/Brain.

questions.q: What happens before Command Center applies an impactful change like new business hours?
options: It applies the change and emails a receipt
It previews the change in a confirmation card and waits for approval
It requires a manager password
It schedules the change for the next business day
questions.explain: Impactful writes are previewed in a confirmation card and the owner must approve before they land.

questions.q: What is the headline figure to use externally for Command Center's breadth?
options: About 50 actions across 10 areas
1000+ actions across 100 areas
230+ actions across ~26 areas
26 actions across 230 areas
questions.explain: The lesson says to say '230+ actions across ~26 areas' externally.

questions.q: How does Command Center decide which part of the product a request belongs to?
options: The owner must pick the area first
It routes the request to the right specialist behind the scenes
It guesses randomly and corrects later
It asks support staff to triage it
questions.explain: Command Center decides the area itself and hands the request to the right specialist; the owner never picks.

questions.q: Which is an example of a WRITE action from the lesson?
options: "How many website clicks have I gotten?"
"How are my reviews trending?"
"What's my active subscription and when's my next bill?"
"Reschedule Friday's 2pm to 10am and text the customer."
questions.explain: Rescheduling and texting the customer changes data, making it a write action.

questions.q: When you tell Command Center to change your business hours, what helpful follow-up can it do?
options: Push the change to your Google Business Profile so Google stays in sync
Automatically refund recent customers
Delete past appointments outside the new hours
Disable the Front Desk agent
questions.explain: It can push the hours change to the Google Business Profile so the listing stays in sync.

questions.q: What is the team's internal rule about confirmations?
options: Confirmation is optional for trusted owners
If it's not asking for confirmation before a change, something is off
Confirmation only applies to deletions
Confirmation is shown only on the first change each day
questions.explain: The team's rule is that Command Center always takes confirmation; if it isn't asking, something is off.

questions.q: What is the design target for data sharing between businesses?
options: Limited sharing for benchmarking
Sharing only with owner consent
Zero data shared across business owners
Sharing aggregated anonymous data
questions.explain: Cross-business isolation targets zero data shared across business owners and is specifically tested.

questions.q: How does Command Center handle payment-card data?
options: It stores it securely for faster checkout
It will not handle or expose card data (PCI refusal)
It encrypts and forwards it to Stripe
It handles it only with manager approval
questions.explain: It refuses payment-card data outright as a deliberate PCI safety feature.

questions.q: When you save a fact through Command Center that conflicts with an existing value, what happens today?
options: It silently overwrites the old value
It ignores the new value entirely
It shows the existing value and asks which one to keep
It auto-catches contradictions from calls and your website too
questions.explain: Saving a conflicting fact surfaces the existing value and asks which to keep, via save-structured-memory returning conflict: true.

questions.q: The internal framing for Command Center is best described as:
options: "Claude Code for salon owners"
"A smarter FAQ bot"
"The Zoca settings menu"
"A voice-only assistant"
questions.explain: The product team frames it as 'Claude Code for salon owners' because it does the action rather than just advising.

questions.q: Where does Command Center live in the dashboard?
options: Only on the calendar page
On every page, via a top-right button plus Cmd+K
Only inside the billing settings
Only on the mobile app
questions.explain: It lives on every page with a top-right button and a Cmd+K shortcut.

questions.q: Which scope description matches the knowledge base?
options: Per business and unique to each owner
Depends on which products are enabled
Global, the same for every business
Only available on full-screen mode
questions.explain: The knowledge base is global static know-how that is the same for every business.

questions.q: Which four broad domains do the specialists cover?
options: Calendar, Email, SMS, and Voice
Scheduling, Discovery/marketing, Front Desk, and Support
Read, Write, Confirm, and Memory
Sales, HR, Legal, and Finance
questions.explain: The specialists cover Scheduling, Discovery/marketing, Front Desk, and Support.

questions.q: Which of these is a READ action?
options: "Reply to my latest review."
"Post an update about my new summer color package."
"Pull up everyone who hasn't booked in 90 days."
"Add a pedicure to this booking and send a deposit link."
questions.explain: Pulling up clients who haven't booked fetches data without changing anything, so it is a read.

questions.q: How does Command Center's memory operate?
options: Per user and reset each session
Per business and shared across the business
Global across all Zoca businesses
Only retained for 24 hours
questions.explain: Memory is per business and shared across the business so it stays consistent regardless of who uses it.

questions.q: How are a business's multiple locations handled in Command Center?
options: Each location needs a separate login and chat
One conversation handles all locations without switching and starting over
Only the primary location is supported
Locations must be merged into one before use
questions.explain: One conversation handles all locations; the owner can ask about one then another in the same chat.

questions.q: What is the relationship between Command Center and Zoca's Brain?
options: Command Center can only read from the Brain
The Brain is a separate product Command Center cannot access
It is a two-way link: Command Center reads from and writes to the Brain
Command Center replaces the Brain entirely
questions.explain: The connection is two-way: it reads Brain facts to ground answers and writes new facts other tools can use.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the real starting point of Discovery?
options: Google Business Profile management
Keyword analysis — what people search and the demand behind it
Building the website
Replying to reviews
questions.explain: The 'UNLEARN THIS' callout says GBP is downstream of keywords; Discovery starts from keyword analysis and demand.

questions.q: How does Discovery fit into Zoca's three-agent model and packaging?
options: It is optional and only included in the full suite
It is sold only as a standalone product
It is mandatory and part of every combination — the wedge
It can be skipped if the customer buys Bookings
questions.explain: Discovery is in every combination — it's mandatory and is the wedge; there is no standalone Front Desk or Bookings.

questions.q: What are Discovery's three SEO pillars?
options: Local SEO, Website SEO, and AI search
Reviews, Photos, and Posts
Email, SMS, and Social
Paid ads, Organic, and Referral
questions.explain: The lesson defines the three pillars as Local SEO, Website SEO, and AI search.

questions.q: When a customer buys more than one agent, in what fixed order are they onboarded?
options: Front Desk → Bookings → Discovery
Bookings → Discovery → Front Desk
Discovery → Front Desk → Bookings
Discovery → Bookings → Front Desk
questions.explain: The 'GOOD TO KNOW' callout states the fixed order is Discovery → Bookings → Front Desk, because Front Desk needs scheduling context.

questions.q: In the correct order, what are the five steps of the keyword pipeline?
options: Demand → Searches → Relevance → Selection → Competitor
Searches → Demand → Relevance → Competitor → Selection
Relevance → Searches → Demand → Competitor → Selection
Searches → Competitor → Demand → Relevance → Selection
questions.explain: The lesson lists the pipeline as Searches, Demand, Relevance, Competitor, Selection — in that order.

questions.q: How should a salon's primary Google category be chosen?
options: By a gut guess about what the business 'is'
By whichever service has the highest price
From impressions, demand, and competition data
Always 'hair salon' for any hair-and-nails salon
questions.explain: The 'DON'T ASSUME' callout says pick the primary category from impressions, demand, and competition — never from a gut guess.

questions.q: What is the difference between branded and non-branded keywords?
options: Branded contain the business or chain name; non-branded describe the service
Branded describe the service; non-branded contain the business name
Branded are paid ads; non-branded are organic
Branded are local; non-branded are hyperlocal
questions.explain: Branded keywords contain the business/chain name (e.g. 'VLCC near me'); non-branded describe the service (e.g. 'hair salon near me').

questions.q: On the Map View, how is rank shown and why are dense scans limited to about 3 per day?
options: A 5×5 grid; limited because of monthly billing caps
A 7×7 geo-grid over ~3 miles; each scan is 49 live Google queries
A single citywide pin; limited by Google account suspension risk
A 10×10 grid; limited because each scan emails the owner
questions.explain: The 'ON THE SCREEN' callout describes a 7×7 geo-grid over ~3 miles, with dense scans limited to ~3/day because each is 49 live Google queries.

questions.q: What are the two calls to action that every Discovery-generated site carries?
options: Email and Directions
Subscribe and Share
Call and Book
Quote and Chat
questions.explain: The lesson states every site carries two CTAs: Call and Book.

questions.q: When does the generated website actually go live?
options: The instant it is generated in the demo
When the trial starts
After the first blog publishes
Only once the owner buys a custom domain
questions.explain: The 'HONESTY NOTE' clarifies the site goes live when the trial starts, not the moment it's generated.

questions.q: Why are Discovery's blogs formatted as questions and answers?
options: It is purely a stylistic preference
It makes blogs shorter and cheaper to produce
Q&A is the format Google and AI engines pull from for specific questions
It avoids any AI-content penalties
questions.explain: The 'GOOD TO KNOW' callout says the Q&A/FAQ format is strategic — it's what Google and AI engines pull from when someone asks a specific question.

questions.q: What happens to a Discovery website when the salon's services change?
options: The owner must manually rebuild each page
The site rebuilds itself to match (a 'website flip')
Nothing — the site is static once published
The whole site is taken offline until re-approved
questions.explain: The auto-rebuild section says the site rebuilds to match when services change — a 'website flip' — so the owner never updates pages manually.

questions.q: What is the most important distinction to get right about AI search?
options: You hold a numbered position like 'position 3'
There is no ranking — only whether you're recommended and cited
Rankings matter more than mentions
Only paid placement gets you recommended
questions.explain: The lesson stresses there is no 'ranking' in AI search — it's about mentions and citations, not a position number.

questions.q: Which four AI engines are active in the Run Audit today?
options: ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overview, and Perplexity
ChatGPT, Claude, Bing, and Siri
Gemini, Perplexity, Alexa, and Copilot
ChatGPT, Grok, Google AI Overview, and Yelp
questions.explain: The lesson lists the four active engines as ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overview, and Perplexity.

questions.q: What does the AEO score measure, and on what scale?
options: Number of leads, scored 0–100
Profile completeness, scored high/medium/low
How strongly the business shows up in AI answers, scored 0–10
Competitor count, scored 1–5 stars
questions.explain: The AEO score measures how strongly the business shows up in AI answers, scored 0 to 10.

questions.q: How is Zoca positioned relative to the enterprise tool Profound?
options: Zoca resells Profound to small businesses
Zoca does for small businesses what Profound does for enterprise
Profound is a generic SEO agency to avoid comparing to
Zoca is built on Profound's API
questions.explain: The lesson frames Zoca as doing for small businesses what Profound does for enterprise companies like Salesforce and Ramp.

questions.q: Why must GBP verification be qualified early in the conversation?
options: Verification costs the owner extra money
An unverified profile breaks the overview screen and disables features
Google bans unverified businesses from search
Verification is only needed for the website, not the listing
questions.explain: The objection callout states an unverified profile breaks the overview screen and disables features, so it's a hard dependency to qualify early.

questions.q: How are collected reviews gated before going public?
options: All reviews auto-publish immediately
Reviews under 4 stars are held internally; 5-star/strong ones publish to the website and GBP
Only reviews left via QR code are published
The owner must manually publish every review
questions.explain: The 'HOW REVIEWS ARE GATED' callout: anything under 4 stars is held internally, while 5-star/strong reviews publish to the website and GBP.

questions.q: On the Photos screen, which three slots does Google score the profile on?
options: Logo, Cover, and Exterior
Logo, Interior, and Staff
Cover, Menu, and Products
Exterior, Interior, and Team
questions.explain: The 'ON THE SCREEN' callout names three photo slots Google scores you on: Logo, Cover, and Exterior.

questions.q: What is described as the single biggest ranking signal on the profile?
options: The number of photos uploaded
Hours accuracy
The primary category
The website link
questions.explain: The lesson states the primary category is the single biggest ranking signal (with hours accuracy as the top trust signal).

questions.q: What are the four statuses an enquiry can carry in the leads surface?
options: New, Contacted, Won, Lost
Booked, Not booked, Unresponsive, Duplicate
Hot, Warm, Cold, Dead
Open, Pending, Closed, Spam
questions.explain: The lesson lists the four lead statuses as Booked, Not booked, Unresponsive, and Duplicate.

questions.q: What is the central reframe of this lesson?
options: Promise a guaranteed monthly lead count
Sell the visible marketing work that produces leads, not a lead-prediction number
Focus the demo entirely on the leads list
Only sell the audit, never the dashboards
questions.explain: The big reframe is to sell the visible marketing work that produces leads, never a lead-prediction number.

questions.q: Where do abandoned booking leads from the Front Desk product appear?
options: Only inside the Front Desk product
They are discarded if not completed
In the Discovery leads surface
In a separate billing report
questions.explain: The lesson explains abandoned leads captured by Front Desk surface in the Discovery leads view.

questions.q: On the Overview tab, why does 'Reviews consistency' measure the percent of weeks with a new review rather than a lifetime total?
options: Because lifetime totals are hard to compute
Because Google rewards velocity, not a lifetime total
Because owners prefer weekly numbers
Because it limits Google API calls
questions.explain: The 'ON THE SCREEN' callout says Reviews consistency is the % of weeks with at least one new review because Google rewards velocity, not a lifetime total.

questions.q: Discovery is best described as Zoca's 'wedge.' What does that mean?
options: The most expensive, highest-commitment product
An optional add-on for existing customers
The lowest-commitment entry product that leads customers toward the rest of Zoca
A product that requires switching booking platforms
questions.explain: Discovery is the wedge: the lowest-commitment entry product (no booking switch) and the on-ramp to everything else.

questions.q: Which statement about AI search is correct?
options: Businesses are ranked at numbered positions
It's about being recommended and cited, not a position number
Only ChatGPT is measured
Citations never reveal competitors
questions.explain: AI search has no ranking — it's about mentions and citations, including which competitors got cited.

questions.q: How does Discovery select keywords?
options: A fixed flat list of a few keywords
By the full service catalog, measuring demand and qualifying by opportunity
Only branded keywords
Whatever the owner types in manually
questions.explain: Discovery looks at the full service catalog, measures demand, and qualifies services by opportunity — not a fixed flat list.

questions.q: What two CTAs appear on every Discovery website?
options: Call and Book
Map and Menu
Email and Subscribe
Review and Share
questions.explain: Every generated site carries both a Call and a Book button.

questions.q: What is E-E-A-T?
options: A pricing tier for Discovery plans
Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness — a content-quality framework
The four AI engines audited
The four lead statuses
questions.explain: E-E-A-T is Google's content-quality framework — Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness — influencing both SEO and AI recommendations.

questions.q: Why is the Brain described as the 'moat' for AI recommendations?
options: It stores billing and payment data
It is a fixed keyword list
It holds genuinely unique business facts that keep content unique and grounded
It blocks competitors from being cited
questions.explain: The Brain stores genuinely unique business facts that keep content unique and grounded — exactly what gets a business recommended.

questions.q: Roughly how many blogs does the content engine publish by default, and how is it framed?
options: 5 per week, fixed
1 per day, fixed
~2 per week, configurable
10 per month, fixed
questions.explain: The default is ~2 blogs per week, presented as configurable — don't quote a fixed '5/week'.

questions.q: When a prospect asks 'how many leads will I get?', what is the recommended response?
options: Promise a specific monthly number
Refuse to give a number and redirect to the visible work and where they stand today
Quote the competitor's lead count
Estimate based on their review count
questions.explain: The lesson advises not to promise a number and to redirect to the visible work on the dashboard and where they stand today.

questions.q: According to Google's Business Profile help documentation, what three factors does Google use to rank local results?
options: Keywords, backlinks, and page speed
Relevance, distance, and prominence
Reviews, photos, and hours
Budget, ad spend, and bid amount
questions.explain: The lesson states Google's own documentation lists relevance, distance, and prominence as the three local ranking factors.

questions.q: Which two of Google's three local ranking factors does a business mostly control?
options: Distance and prominence
Relevance and distance
Relevance and prominence
Distance and intent
questions.explain: The lesson's rule of thumb says you mostly control relevance and prominence but cannot control distance.

questions.q: What does NAP consistency mean in local SEO?
options: Name, Address, and Phone number written identically everywhere online
Number of Active Profiles kept up to date
New Appointments Posted on the profile
Name, Account, and Password matching across sites
questions.explain: The lesson defines NAP consistency as Name, Address, and Phone number written identically everywhere online.

questions.q: Roughly what share of all Google searches does the lesson say have local intent?
options: About 12%
About 25%
About 46%
About 75%
questions.explain: The lesson states roughly 46% of all Google searches have local intent.

questions.q: What is the core mindset shift of AEO/GEO compared to classic SEO?
options: You buy ad placement inside AI answers
You aim to rank #1 in ChatGPT
There is no 'position' to win; the goal is to be included and cited in the AI's answer
You optimize purely for backlinks
questions.explain: The lesson stresses there is no ranked position in AI answers; the goal is to be included and recommended within the synthesized answer.

questions.q: What does RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) describe in how AI engines build answers?
options: The engine retrieves relevant web pages first, then generates an answer grounded in them
The engine ranks all websites then averages them
The engine randomly assigns generated authority
The engine generates an answer first, then retrieves links to match
questions.explain: The lesson defines RAG as retrieving relevant pages first, then generating a written answer grounded in those pages.

questions.q: Per the Princeton-led GEO paper, adding specific statistics to content boosted AI visibility by up to what amount?
options: Up to +10%
Up to +40%
Up to +115%
Up to +200%
questions.explain: The lesson reports the GEO paper found adding specific statistics boosted visibility up to +40%.

questions.q: How do teams measure AEO/GEO success since there is no rank report?
options: Total backlinks earned
Organic traffic from blue links
Page load speed across engines
AI Share of Voice — how often the business is mentioned or cited versus competitors
questions.explain: The lesson explains success is tracked via AI Share of Voice: mention/citation frequency versus competitors across representative questions.

questions.q: What three stages make up the typical AI voice agent pipeline?
options: STT (hear), LLM (think), TTS (speak)
Crawl, index, rank
Listen, transfer, record
Dial, ring, voicemail
questions.explain: The lesson describes the STT to LLM to TTS pipeline as ears, brain, and mouth.

questions.q: What latency window does the lesson cite as the benchmark most production voice agents aim for?
options: 1-2 seconds
2-3 seconds
questions.explain: The lesson cites roughly 500ms as natural, with most production agents aiming for a 300-800ms window.

questions.q: What is 'grounding' in the context of an AI voice agent?
options: Limiting the agent to one phone line
Recording every call for compliance
Feeding the agent the business's real, current facts so answers come from a trusted source, not guesses
Forwarding calls to voicemail after hours
questions.explain: The lesson defines grounding as feeding the agent real business facts so answers are factual rather than guessed.

questions.q: What does 'barge-in' allow during a call with an AI voice agent?
options: The agent to transfer to a human automatically
The caller to interrupt the agent while it's talking and have it stop to listen
The agent to place the caller on hold
Two callers to join the same line
questions.explain: The lesson defines barge-in as the caller interrupting the agent while it talks, causing it to stop and listen.

questions.q: What is 'review gating' as defined in the lesson?

Deleting all reviews older than a year
Requiring login before posting a review
Routing only happy customers to public review sites while steering unhappy ones to a private form
questions.explain: The lesson defines review gating as selectively sending happy customers to public sites and unhappy ones to private feedback instead.

questions.q: Under the FTC's 2024 rule, what is the current maximum civil penalty per violation cited in the lesson?
options: Up to $51,744 per violation
Up to $5,000 per violation
Up to $1 million per violation
Up to $10,000 per violation
questions.explain: The lesson states the FTC can seek civil penalties currently up to $51,744 per violation.

questions.q: What is the single most effective tactic the lesson recommends for ethically generating reviews?

Ask every customer right after the visit and make it one tap
Only ask customers you expect to be happy
Buy reviews from a reputable directory

questions.q: Why can a perfect 5.0 rating with few reviews actually hurt a salon?
options: Google automatically caps ratings at 4.9
It increases the cost of advertising
A wall of nothing-but-5-stars can read as fake and thin counts seem unproven
Customers prefer salons with no reviews

questions.q: Which Google Business Profile field is described as the single strongest controllable ranking lever?
options: The primary category
The business description
The number of photos
The website link
questions.explain: The lesson identifies the primary category as the #1 local pack ranking factor and strongest controllable lever.

questions.q: In 2025, what verification method does Google most often require for a Business Profile?
options: A mailed postcard code only
Video verification — an unedited walkthrough of the business
An email confirmation only
A notarized legal document

questions.q: According to the lesson, fully populated, verified profiles appear about how much more often than incomplete ones?
options: About 20% more often
About 50% more often
About 80% more often
About 200% more often
questions.explain: The lesson states fully populated, verified profiles appear roughly 80% more often than incomplete ones.

questions.q: What is happening to the traditional Q&A tab on Google Business Profiles?
options: It is being expanded with video answers
It is being moved to the website only
It is being phased out and replaced by an AI-generated 'Ask about this place' answer
It now requires a paid subscription
questions.explain: The lesson says the Q&A tab is being phased out in favor of an AI-generated 'Ask about this place' answer drawn from profile data.

questions.q: What are the three stages of how Google Search works, per Google's documentation?
options: Search, click, convert
Crawl, index, rank
Relevance, distance, prominence
On-page, technical, off-page
questions.explain: The lesson states Google works in three stages: crawl (discover), index (understand and store), and rank (order results).

questions.q: What does the 'extra E' in E-E-A-T stand for, added in 2022?
options: Engagement
Efficiency
Experience
Endorsement
questions.explain: The lesson explains the extra E added in 2022 is Experience, rewarding content from someone who has actually done the thing.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about whether Google penalizes AI-written content?
options: AI content is always penalized regardless of quality
False — Google penalizes thin, generic content, not content for being AI-written
AI content ranks higher automatically
Google bans all AI content from its index
questions.explain: The lesson states AI-written content is not penalized for being AI; the risk is thin, generic, mass-produced content with little value.

questions.q: What realistic timeline does the lesson give for meaningful SEO results?
options: 1-2 weeks
1-3 months
4-12 months
2-3 years
questions.explain: The lesson cites a 4-12 month window for meaningful SEO results, describing it as slow then compounding.

questions.q: What is the local pack (also called the map pack or 3-pack)?
options: A paid advertising bundle for local businesses
The boxed cluster of usually three local businesses, shown with a map, at the top of local-intent searches
A set of three keywords every page should target
A Google subscription tier for salons
questions.explain: The lesson defines the local pack as the top-of-page block of typically three local businesses shown with a map.

questions.q: Which two of Google's three local ranking factors are mostly within a business's control?
options: Relevance and prominence
Distance and relevance
Distance and prominence
Proximity and intent
questions.explain: The Local SEO lesson states businesses mostly control relevance and prominence but not distance.

questions.q: What does 'zero-click search' mean in the AEO/GEO context?
options: A search that returns no results
A search blocked by an ad blocker
A search answered on-screen so the user never clicks through to a website
A search performed without typing
questions.explain: The AEO/GEO lesson defines a zero-click search as one answered on-screen so the user never visits a website.

questions.q: In an AI voice agent, what is 'hallucination'?
options: When the agent transfers a call to a human
When the agent confidently makes up a wrong answer
When two callers hear different voices
When the agent records a message
questions.explain: The AI Voice lesson defines hallucination as an AI confidently making up a wrong answer.

questions.q: Which practice both Google's policies and the FTC's 2024 rule push against in reviews?
options: Asking every customer for a public review
Responding to negative reviews calmly
Review gating and suppression of negative reviews
Mentioning the stylist in a reply
questions.explain: The Reviews lesson explains review gating and suppression violate Google policy and the FTC's 2024 rule.

questions.q: What does the lesson identify as the #1 Google Business Profile local-pack ranking factor?
options: Number of photos uploaded
The primary category
Length of the business description
Having a booking button
questions.explain: The GBP lesson identifies the primary category as the #1 local pack ranking factor.

questions.q: Of the four classic search-intent types, which describes a searcher who wants to act now (e.g., 'book gel manicure downtown')?
options: Informational
Navigational
Commercial
Transactional
questions.explain: The SEO lesson classifies 'book/price/near me' act-now queries as transactional intent.

questions.q: What is a 'citation' in local SEO?

Any place online where a business's NAP appears, such as Yelp or Apple Maps
A legal warning from Google about policy violations
A footnote in a blog post linking to the business

questions.q: What is one of the things Zoe will explicitly NOT do?

Collect a payment or take a deposit / card
Recognize returning clients by phone
Detect and filter spam

By a downloaded client app
By the phone number they're calling from, matched to the client list
By voice recognition of the caller

questions.q: How does Zoe's spam shield actually work?

It answers, then tags very short calls and obvious robocalls as spam after the call
It forwards all suspicious calls to a human
It requires callers to pass a verification challenge first

questions.q: About how long does a standard booking call with Zoe typically run?
options: 60-120 seconds
10-20 seconds
4-5 minutes
15-30 minutes
questions.explain: A standard booking call runs about 60-120 seconds; a quick hours question is 30-60 seconds and a messy reschedule can take 4-5 minutes.

questions.q: What is the core differentiator of how Zoe handles bookings?
options: She texts the caller a booking link to complete later
She only works with Calendly
She writes the appointment into the salon's existing scheduler, live on the call
She emails the salon to enter the booking manually

Square and Mindbody
Fresha and GlossGenius
Zoca Scheduling and Boulevard

It's a deliberate feature so most bookings land confirmed instead of stuck awaiting payment
Because deposits are illegal over the phone
Because she can't access the salon's deposit settings

A reverse-engineered workaround
A secure automated assistant set up on the account using the salon's login
A manual data export each morning

questions.q: Who provides and pays for Zoe's dedicated phone number?

Zoca provides and pays for it, and the owner can pick the area code
The salon's existing carrier
Google, via the Business Profile

By replacing all signage with the new number
By using two separate phones at the front desk

A cold transfer to one destination during transfer hours
No transfer is possible at all
An automatic transfer to a call center

About 5 minutes, fully self-serve, 3 steps
About 45 minutes (rarely over an hour), 10 steps
About 2 hours, 7 steps

options: QnAs and Policies
Business Profile and Services
Custom Instructions and QnAs
Services and Policies

Two (male and female)
Unlimited via voice cloning
Six, one per salon type

An AI auto-answers every gap without owner input

A way to clone the owner's voice

Bookings
Activity
Analytics

It exports leads to a spreadsheet for manual follow-up

As a guaranteed result
As an estimate showing the scale of value, used directionally
As the salon's actual measured profit

$349/mo with unlimited minutes
$239.20/mo with 500 voice minutes
$49/mo with 50 voice minutes

Five journeys, decided by how much they pay

The secure automated assistant adds a surcharge

Well under an hour
Around two to three hours

questions.q: Which payment method requires no setup at all?
options: Card on file
Tap-to-pay
In-person card reader
Cash
questions.explain: Cash is recorded instantly with no card processing and works with no setup, while card payments need Stripe.

questions.q: How long do clients typically wait to see a card refund?
options: Instantly
About 5-10 business days
About 24 hours
About 30 days
questions.explain: Card refunds go back to the original card and clients typically see them in about 5-10 business days.

questions.q: What is the difference between checkout and quick-sale?
options: Checkout settles a completed appointment; quick-sale has no appointment attached
Checkout is for retail only; quick-sale is for services
They use different carts and payment methods
Quick-sale requires a card reader
questions.explain: Checkout settles a completed appointment, while quick-sale is a sale not tied to any appointment, such as a walk-in.

questions.q: Which feature is described as 'coming soon, targeting the next couple of weeks' rather than live today?
options: Taking tips at checkout
Cash payments
Retail products, inventory, and gift cards
Applying discounts
questions.explain: Retail products, inventory, and gift cards are launching shortly and should not be demoed as working today.

questions.q: How is the Stripe card reader described as connecting?
options: Server-driven over the internet, paired once
Via daily Bluetooth pairing each morning
Hand-keyed on a separate terminal
Through a USB cable to the computer
questions.explain: The reader is server-driven: it pairs once over the salon's internet through Stripe, with no daily Bluetooth fiddling.

questions.q: What option lets staff demonstrate the reader flow without owning hardware?
options: Tap-to-pay mode
A simulated reader
Cash mode
Payment link
questions.explain: A simulated reader shows the full payment flow for training and demos without physical hardware.

questions.q: What is the defining behavior of an offer in Zoca today?
options: It requires a typed coupon code
It auto-applies to eligible clients with no code
It is applied only by the owner manually
It only works at the front desk
questions.explain: An offer auto-applies to eligible clients based on rules, so the client never types a code.

questions.q: Which two discount shapes are supported today?
options: Buy-one-get-one and loyalty points
Tiered and bundle discounts
Percentage off (up to 99%) and fixed amount off (to a $0 floor)
Percentage off only
questions.explain: Offers support percentage off up to 99% and fixed amount off down to a $0 floor.

questions.q: Which eligibility option targets clients with no prior bookings?
options: New clients only
Returning clients only
All clients
Staff override
questions.explain: The 'new clients only' eligibility targets clients with no prior bookings.

questions.q: What is the offer lifecycle described in the lesson?
options: Open, partially paid, paid
Pending, confirmed, completed
Draft, Live (or Future), Paused, Expired
Created, edited, cancelled
questions.explain: Offers move through Draft, Live (or Future if scheduled), Paused, and Expired.

questions.q: Everything on the Calendar opens in what, so you never lose your place?
options: A new browser tab
A side sheet over the calendar
A full new page
A pop-up window that replaces the view
questions.explain: Actions like editing, checkout, or blocking time open in a side sheet that slides over the calendar.

questions.q: After Zoca's AI books a lead outbound, the lead is marked as what?
options: Pending
Archived
Converted
Declined
questions.explain: When the AI reaches out and books a lead, the lead is marked converted.

questions.q: What is the default grace period before a no-show is flagged?
options: 15 minutes
30 minutes
10 minutes
5 minutes
questions.explain: No-shows are detected after a default 15-minute grace period the salon can change.

questions.q: A no-show fee can be configured as which of the following?
options: A percentage of the tip
A percentage of deposit, a fixed amount, or a percentage of service price
Always a flat $100
Only a forfeited deposit
questions.explain: The fee is configurable as a percentage of the deposit, a fixed amount, or a percentage of the service price.

questions.q: Every booking automatically gets a linked record where deposit, balance, tips, and refunds roll up. What is it called?
options: A ledger
A cart
A sale
A receipt
questions.explain: Each booking auto-creates a linked sale where all the financial pieces roll up in one place.

questions.q: Which states does a sale move through as it is paid?
options: Draft, Live, Paused
Pending, confirmed, completed
Created, edited, cancelled
Open, partially paid, paid
questions.explain: The system tracks the sale as it moves from open to partially paid to paid.

questions.q: For in-person card acceptance, which account must the salon connect?
options: PayPal
Stripe
Square
Clover
questions.explain: Card readers and tap-to-pay run on the salon's connected Stripe account.

questions.q: The killer offer demo described is a slow-day offer that shows targeting, automation, and what else at once?
options: Margin control
Loyalty rewards
Inventory tracking
Gift card sales
questions.explain: The slow-day offer demo shows targeting, automation, and margin control simultaneously.

questions.q: What is the recommended entry tactic for a Type B (skeptical) buyer?
options: Give a wake-up call that the digital shift is real
Open with one hard-hitting fact they don't already know
Show the cost and chaos of juggling 5+ tools
Walk them through a full feature demo immediately
questions.explain: Type B knows marketing exists, so you have ~30 seconds and must open with a fact they cannot already know to spark curiosity.

questions.q: According to the module, why does Google search produce higher-quality leads than social media?
options: Google search carries predefined intent while social is discovery-first
Social media is more expensive to advertise on
Google leads are always cheaper per click
Social media users never book beauty services
questions.explain: Someone searching 'Botox near me' already wants the service (predefined intent), whereas social-media intent is created later and can evaporate.

questions.q: What average customer retention figure does the internal coaching cite across Zoca's users?
questions.explain: About 40% of customers repeat, which is the whole argument for constant acquisition and why marketing is a must-have.

questions.q: What does the 'map pack' refer to?
options: The sponsored ads labelled above local results
The top-3 local listings shown beside a map in Google results
All organic results on a Google search page
The set of AI assistants that answer queries
questions.explain: The map pack is the top-3 local listings beside a Google map; sponsored ads can appear above it and are labelled as ads.

questions.q: According to the narrative, what is the real first step in a business's life-cycle?
options: Booking
Payments
Acquisition
Taxation
questions.explain: Legacy platforms started from booking, but acquisition (getting found) comes first—if nobody finds the business, the booking tool has nothing to do.

questions.q: When a prospect says 'I can write my own content with AI,' what should the AE do?
options: Argue that AI cannot write a good blog
Ask the cornering questions so they reach the conclusion themselves
Immediately offer a discount
Show them the pricing page
questions.explain: Don't argue—ask the cornering questions that expose how much they'd actually have to own, letting them arrive at the conclusion.

questions.q: Which messaging discipline does the module insist on regarding who does the work?
options: Say a team of humans does it to add credibility
Always say an agent does it, not a team
Avoid mentioning who does the work at all
Say a mix of humans and software does it
questions.explain: Saying 'a team does it' lowers the perceived intelligence of the product; always say the agent does the work.

questions.q: How does the module frame an organic lead?
options: It is the core product Zoca sells
It is the outcome of doing marketing, profile, content and reviews well
It is something Zoca resells like a marketplace
It is generated by $20-CPC ad agencies
questions.explain: A lead is what falls out when everything is done well; Zoca builds the durable asset and the leads follow, rather than being a lead-gen machine.

questions.q: What is the rule about payment relative to the demo?
options: Payment is collected before the discovery call
No payment before the demo—the prospect sees the product first
Payment is optional and never required
Payment is collected only after 7 days regardless of demo
questions.explain: The pipeline mandates a fully-loaded discovery call with no payment before the demo.

questions.q: Who owns qualification in the sales model?
options: The full-cycle AE re-qualifies every deal
The SDR owns qualification and the AE does not re-qualify
The CX pod handles qualification
The customer self-qualifies online
questions.explain: The SDR owns qualification; the AE closes and does not re-qualify, the main reason not to close being product rejection.

questions.q: What triggers which of the five onboarding journeys (A–E) a customer takes?
options: The booking platform they already use
The price tier they select
Their geographic location
The number of staff they employ
questions.explain: The onboarding journey is determined by the prospect's current booking platform (API, no-API/browser automation, or full migration).

questions.q: What are the trial and billing mechanics described?
options: 30-day trial, no card required, billed via Stripe
7-day trial, card on file required, auto-charge after 7 days via Chargebee
14-day trial, manual invoicing each month
No trial; pay in full up front via Chargebee
questions.explain: A 7-day trial requires a card on file and auto-charges after 7 days, billed through Chargebee, with a one-per-business contract e-signed first.

questions.q: For objection #5, 'How do you rank on AI SEO?', what is the correct response?
options: Explain the exact ranking algorithm step by step
There is no ranking in AI search—GEO/AEO is about being recommended and cited
Promise a top-3 position within a week
Admit Zoca cannot influence AI search at all
questions.explain: It's a trick: AI search recommends and cites rather than ranking, so you optimize for mentions, citations and trust signals.

questions.q: How should objection #10, 'I don't want AI to answer my calls,' be reframed?
options: Around 'never miss a call'—it catches calls you'd otherwise lose
By offering a discount on Front Desk
By replacing the human receptionist entirely
By saying AI is required and cannot be turned off
questions.explain: Reframe to 'never miss a call'—it catches after-hours, simultaneous and busy-time calls and transfers to you during your hours, so you stay in control.

questions.q: In the audit for AI SEO (#4), which engines' mentions and citations are measured?
options: Only Google and Bing
ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overview, and Perplexity
Only ChatGPT and Siri
Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok
questions.explain: The audit measures mentions and citations across ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overview, and Perplexity.

questions.q: What is the cure for objection #15, 'The content doesn't sound like me, it's generic'?
options: Switch to a human copywriter
Feed the Brain relevant context so the output becomes differentiated
Lower the publishing frequency
Turn off AI content generation
questions.explain: Feeding the Brain real context turns generic output into differentiated content, converting the complaint into a Brain-building conversation.

questions.q: What is the entry tactic for a Type C (overwhelmed) buyer?
options: A wake-up call that the digital shift is real
One hard-hitting fact they don't already know
Show the cost and chaos of juggling 5+ tools and sell simplicity
A full feature-by-feature product demo
questions.explain: Type C feels covered because they pay for many tools, so show the cost and chaos and sell simplicity, cohesiveness and context.

questions.q: Which principle governs how a pitch should open?
options: Lead with features (the 'what')
Lead with the why—the buyer's world and pain—before any feature
Lead with pricing to filter prospects
Lead with competitor comparisons
questions.explain: Why-before-what: anchor the conversation in the buyer's reality first so the product lands harder once they feel understood.

questions.q: What is the one-sentence marketing story when a prospect asks what the marketing does?
options: Leads and conversions
Content + context
Ads and retargeting
Bookings and payments
questions.explain: The story compresses to content plus context, where context is the business-specific nuance that makes content non-generic.

questions.q: How is Zoca distinguished from a marketplace like Fresha?
options: Zoca charges a flat fee per lead-generated booking
Zoca is a lead reseller that rents leads
Zoca makes a business findable rather than reselling it leads
Zoca takes ~10% of every service price
questions.explain: Zoca is not a marketplace or lead reseller; Google is where the search happens and Zoca makes the business findable.

questions.q: What is the nature of the discovery call in the sales pipeline?
options: An optional intro call before qualification
A mandatory, fully-loaded product demo with all agents active
A pure conversion call focused only on closing
A post-payment onboarding session
questions.explain: The discovery call is mandatory, shows the product fully loaded with all agents active, and is not a conversion call.

questions.q: What is true about pricing across the five onboarding journeys?
options: Browser-automation journeys cost less than full migration
API integrations are the most expensive tier
There is no price difference between journeys
Migration to Zoca bookings is discounted
questions.explain: Pricing is the same whether a customer integrates, runs on browser automation or migrates fully, so guide them to the best-fit path.

questions.q: In the support/CX model, who gets a dedicated pod?
options: Every paying customer
Customers paying under $5k
Customers over $5k or on the full suite
Only multi-location accounts
questions.explain: A dedicated pod is reserved for customers over $5k or on the full suite; others rely on Command Center plus the AI account manager.

questions.q: For objection #12, how is Front Desk positioned versus a human receptionist?
options: As a full replacement that fires the receptionist
As coverage, not replacement—24/7, simultaneous calls, after-hours
As a cheaper but less capable alternative
As identical in capability to a human
questions.explain: It's coverage not replacement—24/7, simultaneous calls, after-hours, spam filtering and outbound recovery at ~$99/mo versus a few thousand for a human.
